title: Task groups with input-order results
summary: Fan out a dynamic number of tasks and carry each input index so completion order cannot scramble the result.
triggers: fan out a dynamic batch while preserving the original order
prompts: Double a batch asynchronously and return results in input order.
invariant: Each result is written to its original input position by the parent task.
mantra: Carry the index out; place the value back.
pitfalls: Task groups yield results in completion order.
Child tasks return values instead of mutating the parent array concurrently.
Use bounded inputs to avoid Int overflow when doubling.
